meta.sanitization_statement: Every text value in this file is authored or paraphrased for this corpus. No real person name, no real organization name, no real email address, no Hebrew source material, and no venture-specific content from any live conversation, transcript, or intercept log appears anywhere in this file. Where a fixture's SHAPE is grounded in a logged RCA, only the structural shape is reconstructed (list length, bracket placement, sentence framing); the RCA's own described content is paraphrased with generic sample-project/sample-library placeholder subject matter, never copied verbatim. This is a check performed and recorded, not an assumption: see 238-07-SUMMARY.md for the exact grep patterns run against this file to confirm no real-name/real-org tokens leaked in.
meta.live_log_entries_note: 238-RESEARCH.md measured that all 38 records in the live ~/.mindrian/card-fire-intercepts.log carry the PRIMARY-arm reason (reached-registry-gate-no-card), and running the shipped computeBackstopHit over every one of their output_text values returns false 38 times out of 38 (0/38 backstop fires). Copying any of them into this corpus verbatim would add a vacuously-passing entry today while importing real conversational content and its sanitization risk for zero corpus value. Zero entries in this file carry source:'live-log' as a result; every entry is either 'authored' (a synthetic fixture built to match a measured live false-positive shape) or 'rca' (a structural reconstruction of a shape described in a resolved/open debug RCA, paraphrased, never the RCA's original quoted text).

entries.text: The dispatch behavior mirrors the classic near-decomposability argument [1] and was confirmed again in a later replication study [2] using a different sample corpus.
